step: Bootcamp: Reproduce the Ala-Ala verdict (Ala-Ala vs Gly-Gly in 98% sulfuric acid)
source: Petkowski et al. 2024, Sci. Rep. 14, 17083 (decisions); Petkowski et al., ACS Omega 2025 (the Ala-Ala product)
data: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.11223995, Supplementary dataset S1, samples AA and GG, acid K (98% w/w D2SO4)

AA_signals.label: Ala-Ala signals from hydrogens on carbon
AA_signals.why: Ala-Ala has two methyls and two alpha hydrogens. The two alanines are not in identical places (one at the start of the chain, one at the end), so each methyl and each alpha hydrogen gives its own signal.

AA_methyl_ppm.label: Ala-Ala methyl (CH3)
AA_methyl_ppm.typical_text: a methyl near 2 ppm in this acid

AA_alpha_ppm.label: Ala-Ala alpha hydrogen (the hydrogen on the carbon next to the nitrogen)
AA_alpha_ppm.typical_text: an alpha hydrogen near 5 ppm in this acid

GG_signals.label: Gly-Gly signals from hydrogens on carbon
GG_signals.why: Gly-Gly has one CH2 on each glycine. The two hydrogens of one CH2 sit in the same place and give one signal together, but the two glycines do not (one at the start of the chain, one at the end), so each CH2 gives its own signal.

GG_ch2_ppm.label: Gly-Gly CH2
GG_ch2_ppm.typical_text: a glycine CH2 near 4.6 ppm in this acid

breaks_down.label: Which breaks down in 4 months
breaks_down.later: You check this yourself in Parts 2 to 4, from the spectra.

AA.call_source: the published finding (Petkowski et al. 2024, Sci. Rep. 14, 17083)
AA.close_message: Free alanine is what splitting the peptide bond with water would give, as in 81% acid. In 98% acid the mechanism study reports alaninamide instead: the end alanine's bond to its nitrogen (a C-N bond) breaks, so the first alanine keeps that nitrogen as an amide group (CONH2) and the end alanine leaves as acrylic acid. See Look closer for the alaninamide spectrum.
AA.product: alaninamide (alanine with an amide group, CONH2, in place of its COOH)
AA.product_source: the mechanism study (Petkowski et al., ACS Omega 2025, Mechanism for peptide bond solvolysis in 98% w/w concentrated sulfuric acid; reference spectra on Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.11122291)

GG.call_source: the published finding (Petkowski et al. 2024, Sci. Rep. 14, 17083)
GG.product_source: the published finding (Petkowski et al. 2024, Sci. Rep. 14, 17083)
